newsitem.title: USA: Four vie to succeed U.S. Rep Gibbons in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Four vie to succeed U.S. Rep Gibbons in Florida.

text.p: Tampa voters went to the polls Tuesday to choose a successor to long-time Democratic U.S. Representative Sam Gibbons, who will retire this year.

Contenders include former Tampa mayor and front-runner Sandy Freedman, state House Majority Leader Jim Davis, former state Sen. Pat Frank and Hillsborough County Commissioner Phyllis Busansky. The winner will face Republican Mark Sharpe, who lost twice to Gibbons.
The four Democrats appeared in a televised debate Friday during which all declared they would be in favour of any proposal to deny benefits to illegal aliens.

Frank has based her campaign on opposition to an increase in a local community investment tax, which also was on the ballot Tuesday and might be the issue of most interest to voters. It calls for a half-cent sales tax increase, which would raise nearly $3 billion over the next 30 years for a variety of school, public works and public safety programmes.

The tax increase originally was a intended to build a new stadium for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers of the National Football League, which remains part of the proposal. The team's owners have threatened to move to another city if the referendum does not pass.
